ELiS – WRITING OF SIGN LANGUAGES

Sign languages
can also be written.

ELiS – Escrita das Línguas de Sinais, or Writing of Sign Languages – is a system created in 1998 by Mariângela Estelita Barros to record sign languages such as Libras (Brazilian Sign Language) in writing.

The ELiS font lets you represent the signs of sign languages graphically through symbols called visographemes. In all, the system has 96 basic visographemes organized into four groups.

On this website you can learn more about the project, understand how the ELiS writing system works and try the font for yourself.

Download ELiS

01 / THE SYSTEM

The groups of visographemes.

In sign languages, signs are built by combining visual movements. Together, these elements form a unit of meaning, just as combining sounds forms words in spoken languages.

The visual movements of sign languages that the ELiS font represents are made up of:

  1. Finger configuration: The shape the hands take during the movement. There are visographemes for the shape of the thumb and for the other fingers.
  2. Palm orientation: Where the palm of the hand faces during the movement.
  3. Point of articulation: Where the sign is made. It can be on the head, the trunk, the hand or the limbs, such as the arm, wrist and leg, among others.
  4. Type of movement: How the hands, arms and other limbs behave while the sign is made.

Facial and body expressions also take part in this construction. Together, these elements give each sign its form and meaning.

Each of these four groups is made up of many elements. ELiS represents each of them with a specific drawing, called a visographeme. Combining these drawings makes it possible to represent the signs of sign languages graphically.

03 / ELiS

Character map

ELiS is made up of 96 visographemes divided into 4 groups: fingers, palm, point of articulation and type of movement. Each visographeme is placed strategically on an ordinary computer keyboard.

Visographemes organized according to the “detailed keys beta” chart. All drawings use the ELiS files, version 2.004.

Glyph details

INPUT

Set up the keyboard and check the combinations

Windows

To look up the installed characters, search for Character Map in the Start menu, open the app and select ELiS. Choose the symbol, click Select and then Copy. Paste it in the editor with Ctrl + V.

The Alt codes in this reference use Windows-1252, with a leading zero and the numeric keypad. Hold Alt, type the numbers and release Alt. Turn on Num Lock. Regional settings and the application can change the result; without a numeric keypad, use Character Map or copy from here.

Mac

Open Edit → Emoji & Symbols or press Control + Command + Space. In the Character Viewer, search for the Unicode code shown in this reference, select the character and apply ELiS to the text.

To find shortcuts for your layout, open the Keyboard Viewer from the input menu in the menu bar. Press Option and Shift to see the alternatives. If the menu does not appear, turn it on in System Settings → Keyboard → Text Input → Edit.

One key, one visographeme
  • On the keyboard, uppercase and lowercase letters are different characters in the ELiS font. Pressing q gives a different visographeme from pressing Q.
  • The same goes for accents and similar symbols: à and À, ° and º are different visographemes.
  • Some drawings are formed by a sequence of keys typed together, with no space, such as the contact underlines. See Font features.

Source: character map of the ELiS files. Instructions: codes in Word, Character Map and Alt codes, Mac shortcuts and Keyboard Viewer.

04 / FONT FEATURES

Font features.

Contact underlines

Under a point-of-articulation visographeme, an underline shows that the hand touches the region. The number of strokes shows what that contact is like. See the example of the face:

How to type it

Type an apostrophe ', the number of strokes (1, 2 or 3) and the key for the point of articulation, all together with no spaces. For example: '2Q. Try it on the body.

Which visographemes take an underline

Point-of-articulation keys A–Z, Ç, x, *, #, \, _, @, &, $ and %. The font also accepts the curly apostrophes ‘ and ’, and ª and º in place of A and O.

Repeated letters

The sequences below combine automatically into a single drawing. Type the letters one after another, without spaces.

These are typographic demonstrations. The linguistic use of each combination follows the rules of ELiS.

The visographemes did not join automatically?

Check that the keys were typed in the right order, with no spaces between them. Some text editors do not apply the font’s automatic drawing substitution. If that happens, try the same sequence in this website’s lab or in another app.

06 / INSTALLATION AND USE

Download ELiS

ELiS ON YOUR COMPUTER AND YOUR WEBSITE

Take the writing to your documents.

Regular, Bold, Italic and Bold Italic.
Version 2.004: four TTF files for Mac and Windows, four WOFF2 files for websites and the user guide. Free, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

Download ELiS ZIP · 4 styles · TTF + WOFF2
Before installing

Extract the ZIP to access the files.

  • Windows/Mac: install the four .ttf files. If you already have an older version of ELiS, remove it first to avoid conflicts, and close the programs where you will use the font.
  • For websites: use the .woff2 files in the Site folder. They are web fonts and should not be installed on the computer.

MAC / macOS

Install with Font Book.

  1. Open Font Book.
  2. Drag the four .ttf files into the window and confirm the installation.
  3. Reopen your editor and select ELiS in the font menu.

You can also double-click each TTF file and click Install.

PC / WINDOWS

Install the four styles together.

  1. Select the four extracted .ttf files.
  2. Right-click and choose Install for all users. In Windows 11, open Show more options if needed. Without administrator permission, use Install.
  3. Reopen your editor and select ELiS in the font menu.

Another option: drag the TTF files to Settings → Personalization → Fonts.

01

Choose the font

In Word, Pages or another editor that supports local fonts, apply ELiS to the passage you want to write. For other languages, choose another font.

02

Type the inputs

Use your regular keyboard and check the character map. Capital letters, lowercase letters and accents are different inputs. The font writes the signs; it does not translate Portuguese into Libras.

03

Review and share

Use the editor’s bold and italic styles. To share the look, export a PDF with embedded fonts and check the result. Anyone who edits the document also needs the font.

How to preserve the drawings and combinations
  • Keep letter spacing at zero.
  • Keep contextual OpenType features and ligatures turned on.
  • Avoid “All caps” and small caps formatting, which can change the visographemes.
  • Turn off autocorrect and spell check in the ELiS passage.
  • If a combination does not appear, check the sequence, the spacing and the editor’s OpenType options, and compare with the lab on this site.
The font does not show up in the program?

Close the program and open it again. On a Mac, check that the family is active in Font Book. On Windows, try installing for all users. Web apps may need their own feature to upload or access local fonts.

WHO CREATED ELiS

Mariângela Estelita Barros

Researcher, professor and creator of a writing system for sign languages.

Mariângela Estelita Barros is a professor at the School of Letters of the Federal University of Goiás (UFG), Brazil. She created ELiS in 1998, during her master’s research, and developed the system further in her doctorate, completed in 2008.

Her work also brings the writing closer to literature: she translated Grimm brothers’ tales into ELiS, among them The Frog Prince, The Twelve Huntsmen and The Seven Ravens, published in a digital collection in 2021.

Read the story of ELiS: how a handwritten script became a font

Learn more: Princípios básicos da ELiS, by Mariângela (2016, in Portuguese) · Literature in ELiS in Jornal UFG (2025, in Portuguese).

TO KEEP LEARNING

From writing signs to building texts.

The article Um texto escrito em Libras/ELiS, by Guilherme Freitas, Mariângela Estelita Barros and Eliane Marquez (in Portuguese), presents the foundations of the writing and analyzes an invitation letter produced in Libras/ELiS. The study helps us see ELiS as a resource for producing texts and building meaning.

Frequently asked questions about ELiS

Are ELiS, Libras and the ELiS font the same thing?

Libras is Brazilian Sign Language. ELiS is a writing system for sign languages. ELiS is also the font that draws the symbols of that system on the computer. To write a sign, you need to know its representation in ELiS.

Does changing the font translate a Portuguese word into Libras?

No. The font changes how the characters are drawn, but it does not translate words or sentences. A text in Libras/ELiS has to be written from the sign language and the rules of the system.

Do I need to install the font to use this site?

No. The font already loads in the browser. To write in an editor on your computer, download the ELiS family, extract the ZIP and install the four TTF files. Reopen the editor if the family does not appear in the font menu yet.

How do I find the key for a symbol?

Check the character map: search by name or filter by group. Click the card to insert it in the lab or copy the input. In your editor, apply ELiS to the passage.

Why do letters or little boxes appear instead of the glyphs?

Make sure ELiS is applied to the passage and that the font is installed. On the site, wait for it to load or reload the page. Letters mean another font may be in use; little boxes may mean a missing character. Check the input in the map.

How do I type accents and symbols on Windows or Mac?

The character map brings together the 182 characters encoded in the font. On Windows, it offers codes and guidance for Character Map; on a Mac, it explains how to look them up in the Character Viewer. Shortcuts with AltGr or Option depend on the keyboard layout.

Do capital letters, accents and similar symbols make a difference?

Yes. q and Q, just like à and À, have different inputs. The degree sign ° is U+00B0; the ordinal º is U+00BA. Copy the exact input from the map when in doubt.

How do I make contact underlines?

Type a straight apostrophe, the number of strokes and a compatible input, without spaces: '2Q, for example. It is a combination built into the font, not the editor’s underline command. See Font features for what each underline means.

Why doesn’t a combination form in my editor?

Check the characters and remove any spaces between them. Use the current ELiS files. The editor has to apply the font’s OpenType contextual substitutions; support varies between applications. Compare the same sequence in this site’s lab.

Can I mix another language and ELiS in the same document?

Yes. Apply ELiS only to the passages written in ELiS. Use a text font for the rest. When copying and pasting, check the font of the passage, because some applications keep only the characters.

How do I share a text without losing the drawings?

To share the look, export a PDF with embedded fonts, when the editor allows it, and check the result. To send an editable file, the other person needs the font and a compatible editor. An image keeps the look, but the text is no longer editable.

Why does All show more glyphs than the system’s groups?

The font’s inventory includes support characters, combinations and automatic variants. The 404 glyphs are not 404 basic visographemes. The map filters bring together 182 encoded characters; some sequences trigger other drawings automatically.

Do the body and the animation teach how to make a sign?

The figure helps locate points of articulation. The BONITO animation follows the reading of the writing. Neither replaces a signed demonstration or the study of Libras and ELiS. Use the guide’s references to learn more.
